liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): The Scarlet into Fire transition is smooth and sweet, with Jerry ripping notes in each Fire solo; Reviewer counts the Scarlet/Fire among favorite Brent-era versions; Jerry sings and plays with authority [18][26]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): Each solo section in Fire has its own distinct progression; Jerry rocked back and forth while soloing during Fire, a lasting image for the reviewer [18][24]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Candyman, Row Jimmy and Foolish Heart are named as favorite Brent-era versions [26]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Reviewer rates Foolish Heart as good [24]
- **I Will Take You Home** (1 review): Reviewer singles out I Will Take You Home as not to be missed [27]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the best Stella Blue ever, with a hair-raising Jerry solo at the end [25]

## Setlist highlights

- **Stella Blue Transition**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-06-28.sbd.skankweed.7802.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 168 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1988-06-28.145612.ots.akg460.ackerman.miller.noel.t-flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 160 min [4]
- **gd1988-06-28.141703.OTS.AKG.Ackerman.Miller.Noel.t-flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 160 min [5]
- **gd1988-06-28.fm-mtx.braverman.12187.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 161 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [10]
- **gd88-06-28.fm-matrix.braverman.17956.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 161 min; rated 3.88/5 by 41 [11]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundquality outstanding; Much of the show is marred by sloppiness and feedback, and Phil is low in the mix [23][26]
- **gd1988-06-28.pre-fm.connor.7831.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 20 songs; 161 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [14]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first show, seated fourth row on Phil's side [19]
- Lawn had marshmallow wars and gatecrashers, including a skinny kid tackled on the balcony ramp by an usher [21]
- This was the band's first SPAC show after the 1985 ban, caused by oversold tickets and crashers [21]
- Venue was horribly crowded, with a speaker set up far back near the entrance; fences easily scaled by crashers [22]
- Speakers appeared to surround the lawn, so the music seemed to enter through the listener's feet [24]
- About 15,000 tickets sold but nearly 30,000 people were inside; this was understood to be the last SPAC show [27]
- Rain began during Candyman, but the band carried on and played strongly [27]
- Everyone knew it would be the last SPAC show ever [28]
- Reviewer waited three years to see a live Scarlet-Fire, which did not match this one [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-06-28.sbd.skankweed.7802.shnf**: transferred by Skankweed; source: SBD>MC>DAT>CDR [1]
- **gd1988-06-28.145612.ots.akg460.ackerman.miller.noel.t-flac16**: taped by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: Ray Ackerman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG 460 w/ck63 caps > AKG B18 phantom power unit > Sony D5 [4]. Also: Edited and mastered by Joe Noel from WAV through Audacity to FLAC; Ackerman, Miller, Noel taping credits, AKG 460 mics; Upgrade to shnid 110953 with confirmed lineage; pauses and tape flips in set one were cross faded [4]
- **gd1988-06-28.141703.OTS.AKG.Ackerman.Miller.Noel.t-flac2496**: taped by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: Recording Info: Ray Ackerman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG 460 w/ck63 caps > AKG B18 phantom power unit > Sony D5; Transfer Info: Master Cassettes (Sony… [5]. Also: Taped with AKG microphones, OTS source; upgrades shnid 110953 with confirmed lineage; flips cross faded [5]
- **gd1988-06-28.fm-mtx.braverman.12187.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Peter Braverman; source: FM (matrix): DAT> CD> TrackThief> AIFF> Peak> WAV> SHN [10]. Also: Source was FM, not soundboard as first listed, with DJ talk and a WPYX Albany station ID, now removed [10]
- **gd88-06-28.fm-matrix.braverman.17956.sbeok.shnf**: source: FM (matrix): DAT> CD> TrackThief> AIFF> Peak> WAV> SHN via Braverman (upgrade of prior seeds from this source) [11]. Also: Reviewer's girlfriend taped the FM broadcast at home on cassette, with two tape flips, one cutting most of Masterpiece [28]
- **gd1988-06-28.pre-fm.connor.7831.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Connor; source: SBD>MC>DAT>CDR>Shn [14]. Also: Digitally edited and retracked by Charlie Connor from original shn files supplied by Skankweed [14]

claims.text: The Scarlet into Fire transition is smooth and sweet, with Jerry ripping notes in each Fire solo
Each solo section in Fire has its own distinct progression
Reviewer waited three years to see a live Scarlet-Fire, which did not match this one
Reviewer's first show, seated fourth row on Phil's side
Lawn had marshmallow wars and gatecrashers, including a skinny kid tackled on the balcony ramp by an usher
This was the band's first SPAC show after the 1985 ban, caused by oversold tickets and crashers
Venue was horribly crowded, with a speaker set up far back near the entrance; fences easily scaled by crashers
Reviewer calls the soundquality outstanding
Speakers appeared to surround the lawn, so the music seemed to enter through the listener's feet
Jerry rocked back and forth while soloing during Fire, a lasting image for the reviewer
Reviewer rates Foolish Heart as good
Reviewer calls it the best Stella Blue ever, with a hair-raising Jerry solo at the end
Reviewer counts the Scarlet/Fire among favorite Brent-era versions; Jerry sings and plays with authority
Candyman, Row Jimmy and Foolish Heart are named as favorite Brent-era versions
Much of the show is marred by sloppiness and feedback, and Phil is low in the mix
About 15,000 tickets sold but nearly 30,000 people were inside; this was understood to be the last SPAC show
Rain began during Candyman, but the band carried on and played strongly
Reviewer singles out I Will Take You Home as not to be missed
Reviewer's girlfriend taped the FM broadcast at home on cassette, with two tape flips, one cutting most of Masterpiece
Everyone knew it would be the last SPAC show ever
Edited and mastered by Joe Noel from WAV through Audacity to FLAC; Ackerman, Miller, Noel taping credits, AKG 460 mics
Upgrade to shnid 110953 with confirmed lineage; pauses and tape flips in set one were cross faded
Taped with AKG microphones, OTS source; upgrades shnid 110953 with confirmed lineage; flips cross faded
Source was FM, not soundboard as first listed, with DJ talk and a WPYX Albany station ID, now removed
Digitally edited and retracked by Charlie Connor from original shn files supplied by Skankweed
After a three-year SPAC ban, the band returned on June 28, 1988 for a final outing there
Show ended a three-year ban at SPAC
